audience_note: Describes the mass killing of civilians and prisoners, including executions and drownings; casualty figures vary widely by source.
title: War in the Vendée
summary: From March 1793 western France's Vendée region rose against the Republic, which in February had called for 300,000 soldiers and threatened lot-drawn conscription, amid anger over the revolutionaries' policy toward the Church. World History Encyclopedia dates the fighting to 1796 and says at least 170,000 Vendeans were killed, about a fifth of the population, with the 1794 'infernal columns' killing an estimated 50,000.

uncertainty.note: Sources differ on the start (4 or 11 March 1793) and on the end (1795 or 1796).

as_recorded.value: On 11 March, an army of peasants swarmed the village [Machecoul]; In March 1793

where.modern_name: Vendée, Pays de la Loire, France

importance.justification: Counter-revolutionary war in western France with a very high civilian death toll.

reviewer_note: The 170,000 and 50,000 figures are from World History Encyclopedia alone; EBSCO gives only partial figures. Start and end dates differ between the two pages. Pin is the department centre, not a single battle.
